_about: Hand labels for the assertion heuristic's error-rate measurement. 'asserts_something' is a human judgement, written by reading each function before running the heuristic against it: true when the function would fail if the behaviour under test were wrong, false when it would pass regardless. The 'why' field records the reason so the label can be disputed. Only functions whose name starts with test_ are labelled; helpers and fixtures in these files are not tests.
_positive_class: the heuristic's positive class is 'flagged as having no assertion', so a true positive is a genuinely empty test that was flagged

test_only_calls_code.why: mutates a dict and checks nothing

test_builds_a_value_and_drops_it.why: computes a value and discards it

test_assert_true_constant.why: assert True passes whatever the code does

test_assert_one_constant.why: assert 1 passes whatever the code does

test_vacuous_self_comparison.why: value == value is true for every non-NaN value

test_always_true_predicate.why: len(result) >= 0 is true for every list

test_assert_short_circuited_by_true.why: the or True arm makes the assert unconditional

test_pytest_raises.why: pytest.raises fails if nothing is raised

test_pytest_warns.why: pytest.warns fails if no warning is issued

test_nested_function_asserts.why: assert inside a nested def that the test then calls

test_delegates_to_module_helper.why: the assertion is in _check_nonneg, one call away

test_delegates_to_fixture.why: the assertion is in the checker fixture
